section: Parliamentary committees - PAC, Estimates, Public Undertakings, Departmentally Related Standing Committees, ad hoc
subsections: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman
Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the financial committees of Parliament:
1. Members of these committees are elected annually by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.
2. The term of the members is one year.
3. Ministers are eligible to serve as members of these committees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Members are elected annually by proportional representation through the single transferable vote and hold office for one year. Ministers are ineligible to serve on these committees.
accepted.tq: Identify the true procedural statements and reject the eligibility trap.
accepted.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the composition of the Estimates Committee?
o: 30 members, all elected from the Lok Sabha
22 members, including 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
22 members, all elected from the Lok Sabha
30 members, including 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: The Estimates Committee has 30 members, all of whom are drawn from the Lok Sabha. The Rajya Sabha has no representation in it.
accepted.tq: Use the composition figures to distinguish the three financial committees.
accepted.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the Committee on Public Undertakings?
1. It consists of 22 members.
2. It includes 15 members from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.
3. Its chairman is appointed from among the Lok Sabha members by the Speaker.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Committee on Public Undertakings has 22 members, including 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha, and its chairman is appointed by the Speaker from the Lok Sabha members.
accepted.tq: Check the complete composition-and-chairman combination rather than one isolated figure.
accepted.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

accepted.s: The chairperson of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and is invariably from which political grouping?
o: A party represented only in the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: The Speaker appoints the chairperson of the Estimates Committee, who is invariably a member of the ruling party.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the convention for the Estimates Committee from the Opposition-chairman convention of the PAC.
accepted.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

accepted.s: The three financial committees of Parliament maintain an unremitting vigil primarily over which of the following?
accepted.x: The Estimates Committee, Public Accounts Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings exercise continuing oversight over expenditure and governmental performance.
accepted.tq: Match the collective role with the subject domain of the committees.
accepted.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about parliamentary financial control:
1. The budget exercises control before expenditure takes place.
2. The financial committees exercise control after expenditure has taken place.
3. Parliamentary financial committees replace the budgetary process entirely.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The budget provides control before expenditure, while the financial committees examine expenditure and performance after the event. They complement, rather than replace, the budgetary process.
accepted.tq: Track the time sequence of control and reject the extreme replacement claim.
accepted.sec: Financial committees - PAC, Estimates, COPU: strength, RS membership, chairman

accepted.s: The Public Accounts Committee primarily scrutinises which combination of documents?
o: Election expenditure statements, census reports and Finance Commission reports
Appropriation Bills, Money Bills and constitutional amendment Bills
Annual reports of political parties and reports of the Union Public Service Commission
Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and reports of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
accepted.x: The Public Accounts Committee examines the Appropriation Accounts, Finance Accounts and audit reports submitted by the Comptroller and Auditor-General.
accepted.tq: Use the document-based function to separate PAC work from legislative scrutiny.
accepted.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

accepted.s: In examining government expenditure, the Public Accounts Committee checks whether money was spent:
o: Within the scope of the demand for grant
Only after approval by the Supreme Court
accepted.x: The PAC checks whether expenditure remained within the scope of the demand for grant approved by Parliament.
accepted.tq: Apply the committee’s audit function to a spending situation.
accepted.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an area ordinarily examined by the Public Accounts Committee?
o: Formulation of the original policy itself
accepted.x: The PAC examines execution and the financial consequences of policy, but it cannot examine the policy itself. It may identify waste, extravagance, loss and nugatory expenditure and assess efficiency, economy and propriety.
accepted.tq: Find the option that crosses the boundary between policy execution and policy formulation.
accepted.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Public Accounts Committee:
1. It may take up certain matters on its own.
2. Its recommendations are binding on the government.
3. It examines not merely legality but also efficiency, economy and propriety.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The PAC may take up matters on its own and examines efficiency, economy and propriety in addition to legality. Its recommendations are not binding on the government.
accepted.tq: Reject the legal-effect trap while retaining the two functional statements.
accepted.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): The chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is generally selected from the Opposition.
Reason (R): The selection of an Opposition member as chairperson is a constitutional rule applicable in every case.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: The Opposition chairpersonship of the PAC is a convention followed since 1967, not a constitutional or statutory rule applicable in every case.
accepted.tq: Separate a parliamentary convention from a binding constitutional requirement.
accepted.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

accepted.s: Who is the chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27?
accepted.x: K. C. Venugopal is the chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee for 2026–27.
accepted.tq: Use the precise current-year office-holder rather than a person associated with another parliamentary function.
accepted.sec: Public Accounts Committee - reports, reporting, chairman

accepted.s: Which committee is popularly described as the ‘Ombudsman’ of Parliament?
accepted.x: The Committee on Petitions is popularly described as the Ombudsman of Parliament because it considers petitions on bills and matters of public interest.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive nickname with the committee’s grievance-related function.
accepted.sec: Committee nicknames and reform area

accepted.s: The Estimates Committee is commonly known as the:
accepted.x: The Estimates Committee is known as the Continuous economy committee and suggests economies and alternative policies.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among the committee nicknames instead of matching only by financial subject.
accepted.sec: Committee nicknames and reform area

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Committee — Characterisation
1. Public Accounts Committee — Watchdog on departmental expenditure and irregularities
2. Estimates Committee — Suggests economies and alternative policies
3. Committee on Petitions — Examines only public accounts

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The PAC is described as a watchdog on departmental expenditure and irregularities, and the Estimates Committee suggests economies and alternative policies. The Committee on Petitions deals with petitions on bills and public-interest matters, not only public accounts.
accepted.tq: Locate the single function mismatch in a set of closely related committee descriptions.
accepted.sec: Committee nicknames and reform area

accepted.s: Which of the following groups consists of committees regarded as part of the parliamentary watchdog group?
o: Subordinate Legislation, Government Assurances, Estimates, PAC, COPU and DRSCs
Committee on Petitions, Supreme Court, PAC and Finance Commission
Rules Committee, Election Commission, Estimates and CAG
Finance Commission, UPSC, Election Commission, PAC and COPU
accepted.x: The watchdog group comprises the Committee on Subordinate Legislation, Committee on Government Assurances, Estimates Committee, PAC, COPU and Departmentally Related Standing Committees.
accepted.tq: Check the complete group and exclude constitutional bodies that are not parliamentary committees.
accepted.sec: Committee nicknames and reform area

accepted.s: The Public Accounts Committee originated in 1921 under the:
accepted.x: The Public Accounts Committee originated in 1921 under the Government of India Act, 1919.
accepted.tq: Use the year–enactment pair to avoid confusion among the constitutional reform Acts.
accepted.sec: Origin years and recommending bodies

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Departmentally Related Standing Committees:
1. They were introduced in 1993 with 17 committees.
2. Their number became 24 from 2004.
3. Their establishment was based on the recommendation of the Rules Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: DRSCs began in 1993 with 17 committees, expanded to 24 from 2004, and were introduced on the recommendation of the Rules Committee.
accepted.tq: Combine the origin year, numerical expansion and recommending body in one verification set.
accepted.sec: Origin years and recommending bodies

accepted.s: Which committee considers petitions relating to Bills and matters of public interest?
accepted.x: The Committee on Petitions examines petitions relating to Bills and matters of public interest.
accepted.tq: Match the petition-related function with the exact committee name.
accepted.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched regarding the strength of standing committees?
o: Committee on Petitions: Lok Sabha 15, Rajya Sabha 10
Committee on Subordinate Legislation: Lok Sabha 10, Rajya Sabha 15
Committee on Government Assurances: Lok Sabha 10, Rajya Sabha 15
Committee of Privileges: Lok Sabha 10, Rajya Sabha 10
accepted.x: The Committee on Petitions has 15 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha. The Committee on Subordinate Legislation has 15 members from each House, while Government Assurances and Privileges have 15 in the Lok Sabha and 10 in the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure House-wise strength pair and eliminate the reversed figures.
accepted.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

accepted.s: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation is concerned with:
o: Checking the exercise of delegated rule-making power
accepted.x: The Committee on Subordinate Legislation checks how delegated rule-making powers are exercised.
accepted.tq: Distinguish delegated legislation from assurances, ethics and business scheduling.
accepted.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ethics Committee of the Rajya Sabha was established on 4 March 1997.
2. The Ethics Committee of the Lok Sabha was established on 16 May 2000.
3. The Ethics Committees examine the conduct of members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee dates from 4 March 1997, the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee from 16 May 2000, and their subject is the conduct of members.
accepted.tq: Verify both dates first, then connect the committees to their common function.
accepted.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Committee on Government Assurances — Exercises delegated rule-making power
Business Advisory Committee — Allots time for government and other business
Committee of Privileges — Examines members’ conduct
Ethics Committee — Considers questions of privilege
accepted.x: The Business Advisory Committee allots time for government and other business. Questions of privilege belong to the Committee of Privileges, members’ conduct to the Ethics Committee, and delegated rule-making to the Committee on Subordinate Legislation.
accepted.tq: Find the only correctly assigned function among neighbouring standing committees.
accepted.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

accepted.s: Which of the following committees is chaired by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
accepted.x: The Speaker chairs the Lok Sabha Business Advisory Committee, which allots time for government and other business.
accepted.tq: Use the authority–function relationship to identify the committee chaired by the Speaker.
accepted.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding other standing committees:
1. The Committee on Private Members’ Bills and Resolutions is a Lok Sabha-only committee.
2. The Committee on Absence of Members is a Lok Sabha-only committee.
3. The Committee on Empowerment of Women consists of members of both Houses and was established on 29 April 1997.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The two specified committees are exclusive to the Lok Sabha, while the Committee on Empowerment of Women is a committee of both Houses established on 29 April 1997.
accepted.tq: Check House jurisdiction separately from the establishment date.
accepted.sec: Other standing committees - function, strength, date

accepted.s: The Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes consists of:
o: 31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
30 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 15 from the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: The Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs has 30 members, comprising 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Compare the committee’s 20–10 composition with the similar 21–10 DRSC figure.
accepted.sec: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Committee on Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
o: Reviewing welfare programmes for SCs and STs in Union ministries and bodies
Determining the composition of the National Commissions for SCs and STs
Examining reports of the National Commissions for SCs and STs
accepted.x: The committee examines commission reports, constitutional safeguards and welfare programmes. It does not determine the composition of the National Commissions.
accepted.tq: Find the option that assigns a constitutive power instead of an oversight function.
accepted.sec: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs:
1. A Minister may serve as a member of the committee.
2. It examines the working of welfare programmes for SCs and STs in Union ministries and bodies.
3. It examines reports of the National Commissions for SCs and STs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The committee examines welfare programmes and the reports of the National Commissions. Ministers are ineligible to serve on it, making statement 1 incorrect.
accepted.tq: Apply the common ministerial-ineligibility rule while retaining the committee’s substantive functions.
accepted.sec: Committee on Welfare of SCs and STs

accepted.s: Each Departmentally Related Standing Committee consists of:
o: 25 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
31 members: 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
22 members: 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
30 members: 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: Each DRSC has 31 members, comprising 21 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the DRSC composition from the 30-member SC/ST Welfare Committee.
accepted.sec: Departmentally Related Standing Committees

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Departmentally Related Standing Committees is correct?
1. There are 24 DRSCs.
2. Sixteen are under the Lok Sabha and eight are under the Rajya Sabha.
3. Their quorum is 11.
4. Ministers are eligible to serve on them.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: There are 24 DRSCs, with 16 under the Lok Sabha and 8 under the Rajya Sabha; their quorum is 11. Ministers are ineligible, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Use the ministerial-eligibility statement as the decisive false element.
accepted.sec: Departmentally Related Standing Committees

accepted.s:
The Departmentally Related Standing Committees scrutinise which of the following?
1. Demands for grants
2. Bills referred to them
3. Annual reports of ministries
4. Long-term policy of the ministries
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: DRSCs scrutinise demands for grants, referred Bills, annual reports and the long-term policy of the ministries under their jurisdiction.
accepted.tq: Recognise the full range of DRSC scrutiny rather than limiting it to grants.
accepted.sec: Departmentally Related Standing Committees

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about ad hoc parliamentary committees is correct?
o: They cease to exist once they have submitted their reports.
They are constituted only for financial legislation.
They can be created only by the President.
They continue permanently after submitting their reports.
accepted.x: Ad hoc committees are temporary and cease to exist after submitting their reports.
accepted.tq: Use the life-cycle feature of an ad hoc committee to reject permanent-status claims.
accepted.sec: Ad hoc committees - select, joint committees, JPCs

accepted.s: Ad hoc committees of Parliament are broadly of which two kinds?
o: Inquiry committees for a subject, and Select or Joint Committees on Bills
accepted.x: The two broad kinds are inquiry committees set up for a particular subject and Select or Joint Committees constituted to examine Bills.
accepted.tq: Classify the two categories before considering specific examples.
accepted.sec: Ad hoc committees - select, joint committees, JPCs

accepted.s: A Bill is referred to a Select Committee or a Joint Committee by:
o: A direction of the Comptroller and Auditor-General
An order of the President without parliamentary motion
A resolution of the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Referral of a Bill to a Select Committee or Joint Committee takes place through a motion in the House.
accepted.tq: Ask which parliamentary authority can initiate the referral.
accepted.sec: Ad hoc committees - select, joint committees, JPCs

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Joint Parliamentary Committee investigations in chronological order:
A. 2G spectrum
B. Bofors
C. Ketan Parekh
D. Harshad Mehta securities scam
E. Soft-drink pesticides
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The investigations occurred in the order Bofors (1987), Harshad Mehta securities scam (1992), Ketan Parekh (2001), soft-drink pesticides (2003) and 2G spectrum (2011).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the three middle investigations by year.
accepted.sec: Ad hoc committees - select, joint committees, JPCs

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Ketan Parekh Joint Parliamentary Committee investigation was in 2001, not 2003. The soft-drink pesticides investigation was in 2003.
accepted.tq: Check the event–year pair and identify the swapped middle date.
accepted.sec: Ad hoc committees - select, joint committees, JPCs

accepted.s: Which of the following matters is currently before a Joint Parliamentary Committee?
o: The original 1950 form of the Estimates Committee
Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 relating to simultaneous elections
accepted.x: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, concerning simultaneous elections or ONOE, is currently before a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
accepted.tq: Separate a current JPC matter from historical committee origins and completed investigations.
accepted.sec: Ad hoc committees - select, joint committees, JPCs

accepted.s: Which of the following is one of the other matters currently before a Joint Parliamentary Committee?
o: The establishment of the Ethics Committee in 1997
accepted.x: The FCRA (Amendment) Bill, 2026 is currently before a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
accepted.tq: Identify the current Bill rather than a completed inquiry or historical committee event.
accepted.sec: Ad hoc committees - select, joint committees, JPCs

accepted.s: Which one of the following is also currently before a Joint Parliamentary Committee?
o: The recommendation of John Mathai in 1950
accepted.x: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhisthan Bill, 2025 is currently before a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
accepted.tq: Use the current Bill title as the distinguishing identifier.
accepted.sec: Ad hoc committees - select, joint committees, JPCs

accepted.s: Since their September reconstitution, the average attendance of Members of Parliament at 16 DRSCs and the Public Accounts Committee has been approximately:
accepted.x: The reported average attendance at 16 DRSCs and the PAC was only 53% since their September reconstitution.
accepted.tq: Select the reported percentage rather than an attractive rounded majority figure.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Five meetings of the Departmentally Related Standing Committees and the Public Accounts Committee were postponed primarily because of:
o: A judicial stay on committee proceedings
accepted.x: Five meetings were postponed for lack of quorum, highlighting the effect of low attendance on parliamentary scrutiny.
accepted.tq: Connect the attendance figure with its institutional consequence.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The privilege notice issued by Jairam Ramesh concerned remarks made by which Union Minister about a standing committee?
accepted.x: Jairam Ramesh issued a privilege notice against Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over remarks concerning a standing committee.
accepted.tq: Match the privilege notice with the person against whom it was issued.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes a criticism of the Public Accounts Committee?
o: It replaces the budget and prevents all unauthorised expenditure in advance.
It is a post-mortem check, and frequent use of the guillotine can weaken financial control.
It can examine only the legality of expenditure and never its propriety.
It is a pre-expenditure approving authority whose recommendations automatically bind the government.
accepted.x: The PAC is criticised as a post-mortem mechanism because it examines expenditure after it occurs; frequent guillotine of demands can further weaken financial control. Its recommendations are not binding.
accepted.tq: Contrast post-expenditure scrutiny with pre-expenditure budgetary control and reject absolute claims.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
